title: Maximum Number of Books You Can Take
summary: Given an array of book counts on each shelf, find the maximum number of books you can take from a contiguous section where the number of books taken from each shelf strictly increases.
statement: Given an array of book counts on each shelf, find the maximum number of books you can take from a contiguous section where the number of books taken from each shelf strictly increases.
constraints: books has 1 through 100000 positive shelf counts.
Choose a contiguous shelf segment and positive take counts that strictly increase from left to right without exceeding each shelf.
Return the maximum total books taken.
hints: If a segment ends at shelf i taking books[i], optimal earlier takes decrease by one until capped by a shelf or by one.
Compare transformed values books[i]-i with a monotonic stack to find the preceding constraining shelf.
Sum the arithmetic tail ending at books[i], and add the best compatible prefix when that preceding shelf remains connected.
The nearest smaller transformed value is exactly the first shelf whose capacity beats the backward arithmetic requirement; DP joins the independent prefix and forced tail.
editorial: The nearest smaller transformed value is exactly the first shelf whose capacity beats the backward arithmetic requirement; DP joins the independent prefix and forced tail.

tests.explanation: Taking one, two, seven, and nine from shelves one through four gives nineteen.
The final four shelves permit taking one, three, four, and five for thirteen.
